matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral to its integer value and compute the difference between the left‑hand side and the right‑hand side. This numeric gap tells you how the values must change to achieve equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before generating any stick moves, calculate the integer values of both sides of the equation.
matchstick.example: Leaving the equation unchanged without first noticing that 16 ≠ 32, i.e. never computing the numeric discrepancy.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Enumerate every way a single matchstick can be removed from one character and added to another while keeping both source and destination symbols valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When searching for candidate moves, systematically generate all single‑stick relocations before pruning.
matchstick.example: Treating the whole character ‘X’ (two sticks) as a single removable piece, which violates the one‑stick rule.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, compute how the numeric values of the affected numerals change and compare the net change to the required discrepancy.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After listing a candidate move, evaluate its numeric impact and keep only those that can close the gap.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick that turns V into X (+5) when the needed adjustment is +16, so the move cannot solve the puzzle.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A ‘+’ consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into ‘‑’, and adding a vertical stick to ‘‑’ turns it into ‘+’.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric gap suggests that addition should become subtraction (or vice‑versa), consider modifying the plus/minus sign.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘+’ to ‘‑’ but forgetting that the sign reversal flips the contribution of the operand.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑numeral stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If adding a stick to a numeral yields the exact value change needed, look for a source stick on an operator (e.g., ‘+’ or ‘‑’) that can be moved there.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the required numeric adjustment matches a known single‑stick numeral transformation, search for a suitable operator stick to donate.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from ‘+’ to an ‘I’ to make ‘II’, but forgetting that the ‘+’ becomes ‘‑’ and the sign of the term changes.

matchstick.title: Equation structure preservation
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the expression must still contain exactly one ‘=’, at least one valid numeral on each side, and all operators must remain legal symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after applying a candidate move, verify that the overall layout still forms a complete equation.
matchstick.example: Dropping the ‘=’ sign and outputting ‘X + III’, which is not an equation at all.

matchstick.title: Known single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: Use a lookup of common one‑stick numeral changes (e.g., I→II (+1), I→IV (+3), V↔X (+5), I↔V (+4), I↔X (+9)) to quickly assess feasible numeral modifications.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When evaluating how adding or removing a single stick could alter a numeral’s value.
matchstick.example: Trying to turn I into V by adding a single diagonal stick, even though V requires two diagonals.

matchstick.title: Operator sign change impact
matchstick.principle: If a stick move changes an operator (e.g., ‘+’ to ‘‑’), recompute the affected term with the new sign; the sign reversal can flip the contribution to the total.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a candidate move modifies an operator, recalculate the right‑hand side using the new operator.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘+’ to ‘‑’ but still adding the operand values as if they were being added.

matchstick.title: Single‑stick move feasibility
matchstick.principle: When proposing a stick relocation, ensure the source character can lose exactly one stick and remain a valid numeral or operator, and that the destination can accept the stick and become a valid symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During candidate generation, filter out moves that would leave the source or destination invalid.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from V, leaving a lone diagonal which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Single‑stick relocation constraint
matchstick.principle: A matchstick move must involve exactly one individual stick; you cannot remove an entire character that consists of multiple sticks (e.g., X or V) or transfer more than one stick at once.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When enumerating possible moves, restrict the source to a single stick of a character, not the whole character.
matchstick.example: Attempting to delete the whole ‘X’ (two sticks) from ‘XVI’ to obtain ‘VI’, which moves two sticks instead of one.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a numeral or operator without checking that the remaining shape corresponds to a legal Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After removing a stick, verify that the source symbol still matches a known valid character; discard moves that produce invalid shapes.

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model proposes a stick move but does not recompute the left‑ and right‑hand side values to confirm the equation holds.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recompute the integer values of both sides after applying a candidate move and accept only those that make the equality true.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: In the rush to produce an answer, the model truncates or deletes symbols such as ‘=’ or entire operands, yielding an incomplete expression.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any transformation, check that the output still contains exactly one ‘=’ and at least one numeral on each side.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: When a stick move turns ‘+’ into ‘‑’ (or vice‑versa), the model forgets that the sign of the affected term flips, leading to an incorrect total.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Whenever an operator is altered, recompute the expression using the new operator sign before accepting the move.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes removes or adds whole characters (e.g., deleting an entire ‘X’) or changes the equality sign, effectively moving more than one stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Enforce the rule that exactly one individual stick is relocated; validate that both source and destination change by a single stick only.
